question.prompt: Approve this implementation contract: for recursive directory collection, pytest must not import a discovered __init__.py merely to establish package collection when that initializer does not match python_files; pytest must still discover matching test modules beneath that package, preserve their existing node IDs and test results, and may execute the initializer later only through normal import semantics required by importing such a selected test module. Existing pytest_ignore_collect and collect_ignore exclusions remain authoritative and must continue preventing excluded traversal/import. An __init__.py that matches python_files remains intentionally collectable, and an explicitly passed __init__.py retains its existing collection behavior. The fix may change Package-collector presence and plugin-visible collection topology only for recursively discovered, non-matching initializers; no broader plugin-topology compatibility is required. Acceptance requires a regression test proving that invoking pytest on an ancestor directory does not execute or fail on a non-matching package initializer solely during discovery, while matching tests elsewhere still collect/run; a nested matching test remains discoverable under such a package; configured initializer tests and directly passed initializers retain their evidenced behavior; and existing ignore behavior remains unchanged. Scope is limited to recursive directory collection of Python package initializers under the repository’s existing supported environments and collection model. Excluded are changes to python_files defaults, ordinary Python import side effects caused by importing selected test modules, direct-file collection semantics, ignore-rule semantics, node IDs for collected tests, and guarantees about internal collector topology. Residual risk accepted: plugins depending on Package nodes or hooks for non-matching, recursively discovered initializers may observe a topology change.
